title: CX-MT047-CodexContractTestSuite
clause: Live codex CLI contract suite: method probe, steer/interrupt/resume/fork/approval live tests, generate-json-schema drift check, version-range pin

scope.summary:
GOAL: Prove the whole CX adapter against the REAL codex CLI with a dedicated contract-test suite: app-server method availability probe, live steer-mid-turn test, live interrupt test, live resume + fork test, live approval-request test, a schema-drift check comparing `codex app-server generate-json-schema` output against the hand-authored MT-041 bindings, and a CLI version-range pin. Every live scenario that cannot run because the codex CLI or its login is absent produces a typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF record - a silent skip is a contract violation.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New integration-test target src/backend/handshake_core/tests/codex_app_server_contract.rs (plus a support module tests/codex_contract_support/ for probe helpers, version parsing, schema comparison, and the typed-blocker manifest writer) and a machine-readable result manifest written to the external artifacts root (HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT; never inside the repo worktree). A [[test]] registration in handshake_core's Cargo.toml if required by the workspace layout. No product-module changes: defects found here are routed back to the owning MT (041..046), not patched in tests.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. PRECONDITION PROBE. Before any scenario: locate the codex CLI (Windows: the verified codex.cmd npm shim, resolved through the SAME identity checks as the product path - a tampered/unresolvable shim is a typed blocker, not a skip); run `codex --version` and parse it; verify login/auth state via the documented CLI surface (an unauthenticated CLI is NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF with reason login_absent). Probe results are the first rows of the result manifest.
2. VERSION-RANGE PIN. The suite declares SUPPORTED_CODEX_VERSION_RANGE (semver range constant, single source in the support module, aligned with MT-041's BINDINGS_AUTHORED_AGAINST_CODEX_VERSION). In-range -> scenarios run. Out-of-range -> scenarios still run but every result row is stamped out_of_pinned_range=true AND the drift check becomes mandatory-fail-on-any-diff; a version parse failure is a typed blocker. The pin exists so a green run cannot be silently claimed against an unvetted CLI.
3. METHOD AVAILABILITY PROBE. Over a live app-server child: initialize handshake, then probe each method the adapter uses (thread/start, thread/resume, thread/fork, thread/list, thread/read, thread/rollback, turn/start, turn/steer, turn/interrupt) - a method missing from the server (JSON-RPC method-not-found) is a FAIL row naming the method, because the MT-042 capability snapshot advertises all of them.
4. LIVE SCENARIOS (each one asserting through the REAL adapter stack MT-041..046, not raw JSON): (a) STEER-MID-TURN: start a turn with a long-running instruction, deliver a steer mid-turn via the MT-002-bridge path, assert the SAME turn_id continues streaming items after steer delivery and completes without interrupt - the definitive proof that steering does not relaunch; (b) INTERRUPT: start a turn, interrupt it, assert Interrupted state, truncated-partial items, undelivered-steer return, and that a NEW turn on the same thread then succeeds; (c) RESUME: start thread, complete a turn, drop the client, reconnect, thread/resume with the persisted id, assert history-aware continuation (thread/read shows prior items); (d) FORK: fork the resumed thread, assert distinct thread_id and shared history prefix; (e) APPROVAL: run a turn whose instruction provokes a command-execution approval request, assert the MT-044 bridge receives it, answer DENY, assert the turn surfaces the denial and the ledger row exists with latency; (f) EXEC COMPAT: one `codex exec --json` run through the frozen exec lane incl. `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>` continuation and an `--output-schema` hsk.mt_signal@1 structured exit (MT-046 surface).
5. SCHEMA-DRIFT CHECK. Run `codex app-server generate-json-schema`, normalize the output (stable key ordering), and compare the subset of definitions the MT-041 bindings cover against a checked-in expectation snapshot: (a) definitions used by the bindings that changed shape -> FAIL with a structural diff naming each changed path; (b) new upstream definitions/fields NOT used by the bindings -> WARN rows (recorded, non-failing, in-range); (c) the comparison tool + snapshot live in the support module so CI reruns it on every suite run. This is the CI guard the MT-041 contract names as the schema source of truth.
6. TYPED BLOCKERS + MANIFEST. Every scenario emits exactly one manifest row: {scenario_id, status: PASS|FAIL|NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF, reason?, measured?, codex_version, out_of_pinned_range, started_at, duration_ms}. NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF rows carry a machine-readable reason (cli_absent | login_absent | shim_identity_failed | version_unparseable). The manifest is written atomically (temp+rename) to the external artifacts root. A run where every row is NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF exits zero (environment honestly absent) but the manifest proves nothing was silently skipped; asserting PASS language without PASS rows is prohibited.
7. HYGIENE. The suite is quiet (no foreground windows; HBR-QUIET-001), reclaims every spawned child (no orphan codex processes after pass, fail, or panic - drop guards; HBR-QUIET-003), never writes inside the repo worktree, and bounds every scenario with a hard deadline so a wedged CLI cannot hang CI (deadline expiry = FAIL with reason timeout, child killed).

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the delivered MT-041..046 public surfaces and their live-gated smoke tests (this suite supersedes-and-absorbs their per-MT live smokes as the consolidated live gate; the per-MT smokes remain as fast checks).
2. Author tests/codex_contract_support/: CLI locator (reusing product identity checks via the MT-041 public surface), version parse + range pin, manifest writer (atomic, external root), schema normalizer + comparator, scenario deadline harness with child-reclamation drop guards.
3. Author codex_app_server_contract.rs with the precondition probe and scenarios (a)-(f) + the method availability probe, each through the real adapter stack.
4. Author the schema-drift expectation snapshot from the current pinned CLI version and check it in beside the support module.
5. Run the suite live where the CLI is present; verify manifest rows; run it with the CLI absent (or PATH-masked) to prove the typed-blocker path and zero-orphan teardown.
6. Run proof targets; record outputs.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (no GUI work in this MT)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/** (product modules: defects route back to the owning MT-041..046, never patched from the test suite)
acceptance_criteria: Precondition probe locates the CLI through the identity-verified path, parses `codex --version`, and detects auth state; each degraded precondition yields the correct typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF reason (tested via PATH-masked/absent-CLI run).
SUPPORTED_CODEX_VERSION_RANGE is declared once, aligned with MT-041's authored-against constant; out-of-range runs stamp every row and harden the drift check to fail-on-any-diff (test).
Method availability probe covers all nine adapter-used methods and FAILs naming any missing method (live).
Live steer-mid-turn scenario proves the same turn_id continues streaming and completes after steer delivery - no interrupt, no relaunch (live).
Live interrupt scenario proves Interrupted state, truncated partials, undelivered-steer return, and a subsequent successful turn on the same thread (live).
Live resume and fork scenarios prove history-aware continuation and distinct-fork-with-shared-prefix (live).
Live approval scenario proves the MT-044 bridge round-trip with a DENY answer, turn-visible denial, and a ledger row with latency (live).
Exec-compat scenario proves the frozen exec lane, exec resume continuation, and an hsk.mt_signal@1 structured exit (live).
Schema-drift check: binding-covered definition changes FAIL with structural diffs; unused upstream additions WARN; expectation snapshot checked in (test + live).

Result manifest: exactly one row per scenario, atomic write to the external artifacts root, machine-readable typed-blocker reasons; an all-blocked run exits zero with a fully-typed manifest - no silent skip path exists (tests).
Zero orphan codex processes after pass, fail, panic, and deadline-kill paths; every scenario deadline-bounded (tests).
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake_core --test codex_app_server_contract -- --nocapture  # full suite; absent CLI/login => typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF rows, exit zero, manifest written
cargo test -p handshake_core --test codex_app_server_contract schema_drift -- --nocapture  # drift check runnable standalone for CI
code_surfaces: MT-045 recording rows (consumed for scenario assertions)
MT-046 routing + exec resume + output-schema binding (consumed)
implementation_notes: This suite is the WP's Spec-Realism Gate for the CX group: MT-042's capability snapshot values (Resume/ForkSession/SteerMidTurn/InterruptMidTurn all true) are only as honest as these live tests - the snapshot and this suite must never diverge.

Steer-mid-turn live assertion needs a turn long enough to steer: use an instruction with a deliberate multi-step plan (e.g. enumerate then transform) and deliver the steer after the first item arrives; assert at least one post-steer item shares the turn_id.

The approval scenario must run with an approval-forcing configuration (operator-gated policy, no auto-approve classes) so the request is deterministic; answer DENY so the live run never executes an agent-chosen command on the host.
Schema normalization: sort object keys recursively and strip description-only churn before comparing, so cosmetic upstream doc edits do not fail CI; shape changes always fail.

Keep the manifest schema aligned with the mechanically-readable proof conventions used by prior WPs (scenario_id/status/measured pattern, cf. WP-KERNEL-012 perf_manifest.json precedent) so validators parse it without bespoke tooling.
PATH-masking for the absent-CLI test must not mutate user environment; use a scoped child environment.
Live scenarios consume real Codex quota; keep prompts minimal and bound turn counts (<= 2 turns per scenario).

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless contract-test MT: no operator-visible surface changed; the result manifest + recorded FR rows are the TraceProjection evidence per HBR-VIS-004.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Test-surface MT: no product behavior change; lane documentation is owned by MT-043/MT-044/MT-046. If the UserManual artifact is absent in the implementation worktree, record DEFERRED-with-reason per HBR-MAN-001.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Scenario assertions read the FR rows recorded by MT-045; the suite itself proves the FR wiring live.
Recorded DEFERRED-with-reason if internal_diagnostics is not present in the implementation worktree at claim time; never silently skipped.
Suite children are deadline-bounded and drop-guard reclaimed; external-watcher registration deferred to the MT-005 supervisor integration; recorded, never silently skipped.

risk_if_missed: The CX adapter ships proven only against fakes: capability over-claims (steer/resume/fork/approvals) surface in production sessions, upstream codex schema drift lands as runtime parse failures, and silent skips masquerade as green - the exact deflection class this WP's gates exist to prevent.

risks: RISK-1: Silent skip laundering - absent CLI/login turning live scenarios into quiet no-ops that read as green.
RISK-2: Drift blindness - upstream codex schema changes to binding-covered definitions landing unnoticed until production parse failures.
RISK-3: Steer-proof fake - a steer test that would also pass under interrupt+relaunch semantics proves nothing about mid-turn injection.
RISK-4: Version laundering - a green run against an unvetted CLI version claimed as contract proof.
RISK-5: Suite-induced host damage or litter - live approval scenarios executing agent-chosen commands, or wedged/orphaned codex children after failures.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): One-row-per-scenario manifest with typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF reasons; all-blocked run test proves no silent path; PASS language without PASS rows prohibited.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): generate-json-schema comparison with checked-in expectation snapshot; binding-covered changes FAIL with structural diffs; standalone CI proof target.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Assertion requires post-steer items on the SAME turn_id with no intervening turn.started/interrupt - relaunch semantics cannot satisfy it.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Version-range pin stamped on every row; out-of-range hardens drift to fail-on-any-diff.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Approval scenario answers DENY only; every scenario deadline-bounded with kill + drop-guard reclamation; zero-orphan test across pass/fail/panic/deadline paths (HBR-QUIET-003).
